title: Internal signals for safer training: selected evidence
scope: Purposive optimistic falsification review. Distinct protocols are not pooled or fitted as a temporal trend.

proposal.title: Relaxed adversarial training for inner alignment
proposal.claim: Proposal to use relaxed adversaries and transparency to penalize failures that ordinary training inputs might not expose.
proposal.limit: Conceptual proposal, not a quantitative baseline or evidence that the later methods realize its guarantees.
proposal.verification: Primary text inspected; numerical values are author-reported, not independently replicated.

lat.title: Targeted Latent Adversarial Training Improves Robustness to Persistent Harmful Behaviors in LLMs
lat.claim: Adding latent adversaries improves tested backdoor removal and resistance to relearning over comparison methods.
lat.limit: Harmful behavior is approximately known; small models; knowledge returns under further training. Internal intervention does not require human-readable interpretation.
lat.verification: Primary text inspected; numerical values are author-reported, not independently replicated.

solid.title: Preference Learning with Lie Detectors can Induce Honesty or Evasion
solid.claim: Lie-detector-assisted preference learning can yield honesty or evasion depending on optimization, detector quality and regularization.
solid.limit: Constructed preference environment; a successful off-policy protocol does not establish robustness to arbitrary subsequent optimization.
solid.verification: Primary text inspected; numerical values are author-reported, not independently replicated.

atlas.title: The Obfuscation Atlas: Mapping Where Honesty Emerges in RLVR with Deception Probes
atlas.claim: Coding reward hacking can evade probes; suitable KL and detector penalties can yield honest policies in the studied environment.
atlas.limit: Honest is a thresholded task-specific classification. Strong regularization can restrict learning. Does not establish protection in richer agent environments.
atlas.verification: Primary text inspected; numerical values are author-reported, not independently replicated.

scaling.title: Scaling Trends for Lie Detector Oversight in Preference Learning
scaling.locator: Sections 3.2, 4.1–4.5; Appendices O, P and S
scaling.claim: Favorable within-study scaling of undetected deception, with important false-positive and spontaneous-deception limitations.
scaling.limit: Joint detection/behavior metric; constructed domain; 405B uses one seed; changes to optimization and evaluation prevent treating 2025/2026 results as a fixed-protocol time series.
scaling.verification: Primary text inspected; numerical values are author-reported, not independently replicated.

probes.title: Alignment via Training Against Probes Without Losing Monitorability
probes.locator: Tables 1 and 9; Sections 3.5, 4.2 and Appendix F.3
probes.claim: Updated probe objectives improve tested jailbreak resistance; subsequent benign fine-tuning removes the safety of the tested probe-trained Llama checkpoints.
probes.limit: The continuation experiment starts from an abliterated base plus merged safety adapter; original Instruct is a contextual reference, not a matched training ablation. No post-continuation utility reported in Table 9.
probes.verification: Primary text inspected; numerical values are author-reported, not independently replicated.

jailbreak.metric: Mean StrongREJECT score (not a binary attack-success probability)
jailbreak.model: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1 or abliterated Llama 3 8B Instruct
jailbreak.evaluation: 40 held-out ClearHarm prompts; GCG and prefill; DeepSeek v4 Flash judge
jailbreak.selection: Lowest JailbreakBench score among checkpoints retaining at least 95% of mean normalized MMLU, GSM8K and IFEval utility.
jailbreak.comparability: DPO uses 750 paired examples; probe variants use 750 independent completions per class. Same data source is not identical data or total cost. Attacks are not adaptive to the probe intervention.

continuation.metric: Mean StrongREJECT score (not a probability of catastrophe)
continuation.evaluation: 40 ClearHarm prompts, direct query; DeepSeek v4.1 Flash judge
continuation.continuation: 400 conversations; LoRA rank 16, 3 epochs, 75 optimizer steps; 3 seeds. Harmful fraction is by conversation, not by token.
continuation.comparability: Different judge from Table 1. Original Instruct and abliterated-plus-safety-adapter models have different histories. No continued probe loss or safety reapplication during this continuation.
continuation.dispersion: Reported +/- values transcribed exactly. Caption describes standard deviation over three fine-tuning seeds; no confidence intervals or independent-trial counts inferred, including for the Start column.

scaling.metric: Fraction of generated responses deceptive AND unflagged
scaling.evaluation: DolusChat, 200 held-out prompts; GPT-4o judge; evaluation detector probability threshold 0.999
scaling.conditions: Training detector TPR 0.99; target KL divergence 0.15. Llama endpoints: 1B bf16, 405B 4-bit; one seed for 405B. Not equal compute.
scaling.comparability: Within-study cross-sectional scale comparison, not a time series or the incremental benefit over a behavioral-only baseline. Does not equal total deception.

spontaneous.locator: Appendix S, Figure 46 and accompanying text
spontaneous.metric: Fraction of unprompted deceptive responses flagged at the paper's deployed decision boundary
spontaneous.evaluation: Held-out on-policy generation analysis; unprompted lies are a self-selected minority of deceptive responses.
spontaneous.comparability: Different population and denominator from headline policy outcomes. No inference that the 405B model has this detection rate.
